newsitem.title: JAPAN: Poll shows drop in Japan cabinet's popularity.
newsitem.headline: Poll shows drop in Japan cabinet's popularity.

text.p: The rate of support for Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto's cabinet has dropped to 44.2 percent, the lowest level since he formed his first government a year ago, an opinion poll showed on Wednesday.
The poll by the Yomiuri Shimbun newspaper, conducted last Sunday and Monday, showed a 7.6 percentage point drop in support from a similiar poll a month earlier.
Hashimoto"s first cabinet in January 1996 was a coalition grouping his conservative Liberal Democratic Party (LDP), the Socialists and the Sakigake Party, an LDP splinter group.
The LDP returned to sole power in Lower House elections last October.
A Yomiuri poll showed a 56.5 percent approval rating for the first cabinet Hashimoto formed after the October election.
In last month"s poll, support for the cabinet had dropped to 51.8 percent.

The Yomiuri said the decline in support "appears to indicate the public's growing concern for the country's economy, particularly concerning the plunging stock market and the depreciation of the yen".
The Yomiuri report on the poll did not give comparative approval ratings for Hashimoto"s first cabinet. The latest survey covered 3,000 people, of whom just over 2,000 responded.
